title: Pinecrest Retail - Security & Deployment Inventory
summary: Intro discovery on Pinecrest's security requirements for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Covered SOC 2/ISO requirements, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs/retention, KMS/encryption options, and data residency. Agreement to share SOC2 report and a config playbook; Pinecrest to scope POC for Dedicated with KMS integration.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
action_items: Maya - Send latest SOC2 Type II report + ISO27001 summary and security pack link - due 2026-02-09
Liam - Provide draft Dedicated-POC architecture diagram with KMS flow and network outline - due 2026-02-12
Daniel - Share Pinecrest's retention policy and list of compliance docs requested internally - due 2026-02-10
next_steps: Schedule Dedicated POC kickoff (1 week prep)
Redwood to provision sample Dedicated config with customer KMS integration for testing
Customer to run security questionnaire and prepare vendor security page items
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-05 16:30 UTC | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Redwood CSM), Aisha Rahman (Pinecrest Head of AI), Daniel Morris (Pinecrest Security Lead), Priya Kapoor (Infrastructure), Tom Ellis (Ops)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Liam is our solutions engineer, Rina from CSM listening in. How's everybody doing?
[00:07] Aisha: Good, thanks. Busy week but glad we could carve this out — we want to make sure security is front and center before we talk numbers.
[00:12] Daniel: Yeah, got the checklist here. We're mainly evaluating hosted first for speed but likely leaning Dedicated or Private for PII/transactional throughput.
[00:20] Liam: Makes sense. Today we planned to run through SOC2/ISO posture, SSO and RBAC, encryption/KMS patterns, audit logs and retention, and then deployment tradeoffs. We'll note any gaps and propose POC next steps.
[00:31] Priya: Quick callout — Pinecrest processes payment tokens and PII from loyalty program. Data residency in US only is a must.
[00:38] Maya: Noted. We'll highlight region controls and also our private options.

[00:50] [Topic: SOC2 / ISO]
[00:52] Maya: To start with SOC 2 — we are SOC 2 Type II, report available for NDA. We also have an ISO27001 summary. I can send both.
[00:58] Daniel: When you say "available for NDA" — what data is redacted? We need the full report for our procurement team.
[01:06] Maya: Full unredacted can be shared under our standard NDA / secure link. We'll push via secure transfer. Also we maintain audit trails and penetration test summaries.
[01:15] Daniel: Okay. Also curious about continuous compliance — are there automated checks, or is it point-in-time?
[01:21] Liam: Mostly point-in-time attestation, but our infra team runs weekly control scans, configuration checks, and we keep logs for SOC processes. For Dedicated/Private we provide more direct access to logs and configs.

[01:40] [Topic: SSO / SAML & RBAC]
[01:42] Aisha: For SSO we use Okta and also have an Azure AD tenant for contractors. We need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Any gaps?
[01:49] Liam: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. For Hosted we map roles through SCIM with RBAC applied at the token-level. For Dedicated we can integrate directly with customer IdP and federate access into the private control plane.
[02:05] Priya: How granular is the RBAC? Can we do service-level roles vs org-level? We want SOC-like separation for ops vs model access.
[02:12] Liam: Yes, role granularity supports admin, developer, auditor, read-only routes. We also support token-scoped entitlements so you can segment by app/route. There's an API for role sync too.
[02:21] Tom: Are audit logs showing failed SSO attempts, token minting, and KMS key usage? We need that for security investigations.
[02:28] Liam: Yes — audit logs include auth events, token issuance, and administrative actions. KMS calls are logged as well but some of that is in the customer's KMS logs when using customer-managed keys.

[02:48] [Topic: Audit Logs & Retention]
[02:50] Daniel: What retention windows do you support by default? We typically keep 7 years for payment-related metadata, but might tier it.
[02:58] Maya: Default hosted retention is 90 days for full logs, 1 year for aggregated metrics. For enterprise Dedicated/Private, retention is configurable — we support export to your SIEM or long-term storage.
[03:10] Daniel: Are logs tamper-evident? We want to ensure chain-of-custody for investigations.
[03:15] Liam: We can enable append-only storage and forward to an external log store (e.g., Splunk, S3 with object locking). Redwood's console marks events with immutable IDs but for full tamper-evidence we recommend forwarding to your KMS-backed storage or third-party logging.

[03:33] [Topic: Encryption & KMS]
[03:35] Priya: Key question — can we bring our own keys (BYOK) and integrate with our AWS KMS/HSM?
[03:40] Liam: Yes. For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM. Keys never leave your KMS; Redwood uses envelope encryption. For hosted we offer a managed KMS but we also have a BYOK path for Enterprise customers.
[03:53] Daniel: How does key rotation work in POC/demo? We need a predictable rotation and validation plan.
[03:58] Liam: Rotation is customer-controlled in KMS. We provide tooling to rewrap and re-encrypt cached artifacts and a validation script to confirm vaulted keys are used. We'll include the rotation checklist in the playbook.

[04:18] [Topic: Data residency & model caching]
[04:20] Aisha: We also need to know where KV cache and temporary logs live. Are any payloads ever processed outside the US region?
[04:26] Maya: By default hosted customers are routed to nearest region but you can pin region. For Dedicated/Private you pick region and we ensure processing stays within that boundary. KV cache can be configured to persist in-region only.
[04:35] Aisha: Good — can you provide the exact list of regions and data center providers? Procurement wants the mapping.
[04:41] Maya: Yes, we'll attach a region map doc with the pack.

[04:50] [Topic: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs]
[04:52] Tom: From a cost and ops standpoint — hosted is easiest, dedicated gives predictable throughput, private gives us the isolation we need. What are the differences in access to logs and configuration?
[05:02] Liam: Hosted is limited to API-level logs with aggregated metrics; Dedicated opens up more direct metrics, per-token traces, and configs. Private gives you a control plane in your VPC and full access to logs and node-level telemetry. Also private has longer lead times but supports air-gapped setups if needed.
[05:16] Daniel: For regulatory needs we likely need Private or VPC-backed Dedicated. What's your typical SLA on Dedicated?
[05:22] Maya: We provide SLA-backed latency and uptime for Dedicated. We can share the SLA terms and examples in the security pack.

[05:40] [Topic: Procurement & questionnaire]
[05:42] Daniel: We'll be running a security questionnaire — pen tests, last incident summary, encryption details, DR plan — can you fill that out?
[05:48] Maya: Absolutely. We have a security questionnaire bundle we fill out; I'll include it with the SOC2 docs. For any sensitive Qs we can set up a follow-up with our security team.

[06:00] [Questions from customer]
[06:02] Priya: Is there a way to keep payloads encrypted in memory for the hot KV cache?
[06:06] Liam: We don't yet support memory-level encryption for live KV in all runtimes; we encrypt at-rest and in-transit and support automatic purging policies. For high-security POCs we can discuss mobile HSM-backed cache or in-process encryption. There may be performance tradeoffs.
[06:22] Aisha: Any limitations on redaction for PII at the API level?
[06:26] Liam: We have optional automatic redaction hooks and pre-processing filters; for strict needs we advise customer-side preprocessing or data tokenization before sending.

[06:38] [Wrap-up & next steps]
[06:40] Maya: To recap — we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts under NDA, include a region map, security pack, and an architecture draft for Dedicated with KMS flow. We'll also send the security questionnaire.
[06:50] Daniel: Sounds good. We'll review and aim to have internal sign-off on the questionnaire in two weeks. We might kick off a Dedicated POC after that.
[06:58] Maya: Great. I'll follow up with calendar invite for POC kickoff and the docs. Any final questions?
[07:04] Tom: Nope, thanks.
[07:05] Aisha: Thanks everyone.
[07:07] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes: small transcription artifacts present — speaker overlaps at ~02:00 and ~05:30, some proper nouns may be mis-typed (e.g., Okta spelled as "Okta" sometimes transcribed as "Okter").
